clue.text: A defence against attacks and war, I shall need rebuilding

indicators.note: something that needs rebuilding is to be put together again in a new form, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vows to rebuild a defensive structure against raids and warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR turned the pronoun I into the figure 1; the page prints I. 'need rebuilding' rearranges AND WAR I SHALL, twelve letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor's wall across northern England was built as a barrier against raiding tribes from the north.

clue.text: Depend on despicable fellow to be sneaky

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so the despicable fellow comes below

parts.note: to hang on means to depend, so hang means depend
a dog is a contemptible man

explanation.surface: A rogue relies on underhand methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangdog describes a shamefaced, furtive look, as of someone caught out.

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it but its final letter

parts.note: the it of the clue refers back to dot itself
wry means twisted or contorted

explanation.surface: A tiny mark, mostly twisted out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot' is the old word for a marriage portion; 'it' points back to the same word, cut short to DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dot is an archaic term for the property a bride brings to her marriage.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the better word goes around the other

one's stands for one is, which is I plus S

explanation.surface: A person's improvement comes without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'one's' is read as 'one is', not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to make up something on the spot.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
in means the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: Someone protests that nobody ever gets caught up Down Under.

explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is to catch or arrest them.

parts.note: reads as demotion in rank, but describes a London terminus whose name splits into liquid and a lavatory

explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is a London railway terminus, and its name parses as flowing liquid plus a toilet.

parts.note: to lap is to wrap or cover
Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A failure to cover the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, giving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To lapse is to fail, slip or fall away.

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the professional word
almost means the last letter is missing

parts.note: an expert is a professional
Lor! is an old exclamation of surprise, like fancy that!

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is the exclamation LOR, which goes 'interrupting' EXPER, EXPERT 'almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: An explorer investigates unknown places, a kind of field researcher.

clue.text: The ore is transported to this place

indicators.note: when the ore is transported it is moved about, so its letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: The ore is shipped here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is an old formal word meaning to this place or matter.

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it, so the run comes after green

parts.note: green means inexperienced, new
a sprint is a fast run

explanation.surface: A dash across a fresh lawn, or a paper sheet of some sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the cheap paper newspapers are printed on.

parts.note: pix is the clipped informal plural of pictures
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A child's tiny drawings turn out to show a sprite.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixie is a small mischievous sprite of folklore, a kind of fairy.

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

definitions.meaning: a high-ranking bureaucrat, originally in imperial China

O is a ring by its shape

parts.note: to con is to study

explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means marked by luxury and moral decline.

clue.text: Go back without creed I abandoned — I could see through it

back means the word for go is read in reverse

parts.note: zip means energy or go

parts.note: the Nicene Creed is the Christian statement of faith

explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ZIP into PIZ, which goes 'without' (outside) NCENE, the Nicene Creed with I 'abandoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pince-nez are clip-on spectacles with no side arms, lenses a wearer looks through.

explanation.definitionFit: To purse your lips is to gather them into wrinkles.

indicators.note: to reform is to be remade in a new shape, so the letters of warned are rearranged

clue.text: Remove bird breaking open the flower
